title: Make history check handle stray second root and run via athena-cli
summary: The full-history check must not fail on the parentless commit 64ecdc9a (and ff2aafa built on it), by exempting it by full id in athena.toml and testing a second-root history. A gate change must pass the history check under its own candidate gate, and acceptance uses `cargo run -p athena-cli -- check --history`, since bare `cargo run` cannot pick a binary.

defaults_applied.how: New tests in history.rs cover a second root and a child built on it; cargo test, clippy and fmt must be clean.
Behavior criteria name commands the verifier can run, using -p athena-cli.
The exemption lives in athena.toml, which the gate enforces, rather than in prose.
One focused change: the exemption, the candidate-gate judgment, and tests.
The athena.toml comment says what the stray root is and why it is exempt.

assumptions: Exempting the stray root by full id in athena.toml [history] exempt is the simplest handling; the exemption rule (D60) requires the exempt commit to already be in the adding commit's history, which holds for the tip.
ff2aafa needs its own exemption only if the check flags it independently of its root; the producer should run the history check and add only the ids actually flagged.

The history check must judge a commit that changes the gate (athena-gate or athena.toml) with that commit's own candidate gate, and the producer should find how Judged::new picks its configuration and make the history path agree with the landing path.

The runnable acceptance command is `cargo run -p athena-cli -- check --history`; the binary is named athena in crates/athena-cli, and the workspace has several binaries (xtask, athena), so bare `cargo run` fails.

acceptance_criteria.text: athena.toml `[history] exempt` lists the full id 64ecdc9aa4fd24cbe4d4884c864d7e9041585c3d (and ff2aafa's full id only if the check flags it on its own), each with a comment saying it is a stray second root written during job ezm8. athena.toml is a governance file named in this criterion.

A test in crates/athena-gate/src/history.rs builds a history with a second parentless commit and a child built on it. It shows check_history handles them: an exempt root is not flagged, and a non-exempt second root is still flagged.

A test shows a commit that changes the gate is judged by its own candidate gate in the history check, and that a hand change on a non-exempt commit is still flagged. No rule is weakened for ordinary commits.
Run `cargo test -p athena-gate`: the new tests and all existing history, exemption and landing tests pass.
Run `cargo run -p athena-cli -- check --history` from the repo root: it starts (no 'could not determine which binary' error) and does not report 64ecdc9aa4fd or ff2aafa as violations.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check`; both are clean.

out_of_scope: Rewriting or removing the stray commits from history
Changes to records/ or the owner's files
Changing how Athena's commit path writes commits, unless the producer finds the root cause is in this repository's code and the fix is small
departures: The reference is adjusted upward: this is a third attempt, the gate-change rule touches the judgment path, and the work needs a multi-root git test fixture. Cost and time are higher and verification is less likely to pass.
